items.title: Serum creatinine- and cystatin C-derived sarcopenia-related indices and the risk of all-cause mortality in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
items.abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as an important predictor of adverse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). However, the prognostic relevance of sarcopenia-related indices derived from serum creatinine and cystatin C in patients undergoing TAVI has not been fully established. This prospective study included 465 patients who underwent TAVI for symptomatic aortic stenosis. Associations between sarcopenia-related indices and all-cause mortality were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards models, and restricted cubic spline analysis (RCS). Predictive performance and incremental prognostic value were compared across indices using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves (ROC), the Harrell's C-index, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to examine the robustness of the findings. During a median follow-up of 2.8 years, 59 (12.7%) deaths occurred. In the fully adjusted Cox model, each 1-standard deviation increase in eGFRcys/eGFRcr (HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.11-0.75; p  = 0.011) and Cr * eGFRcys (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.14-0.64; p  = 0.002) was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality. Time-dependent ROC indicated that Cr * eGFRcys had the most favorable predictive performance among the evaluated indices. Adding Cr * eGFRcys to the fully adjusted model increased the concordance index from 0.696 to 0.736 and significantly improved risk reclassification and discrimination (NRI: 0.437, 95% CI 0.171-0.704, p  = 0.001; IDI: 0.026, 95% CI 0.004-0.048, p  = 0.022). Findings from subgroup and sensitivity analyses were broadly consistent. Among patients with symptomatic aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI, lower eGFRcys/eGFRcr and Cr * eGFRcys were associated with a higher risk of all-cause mortality after the procedure. Notably, Cr * eGFRcys showed stronger prognostic value and may provide additional prognostic information for risk stratification in patients undergoing TAVI.

items.title: Lower atmospheric pressure is associated with shallower radiofrequency ablation lesions and more frequent steam pops: an ex vivo porcine study.
items.abstract: Atmospheric pressure affects the boiling point of water and may influence thermal lesion formation during radiofrequency (RF) ablation. However, whether atmospheric pressure alters RF lesion formation and steam-pop risk under fixed ablation index (AI) targets remains unknown. A total of 360 analyzable lesions were created in 36 ex vivo porcine hearts using the same RF ablation system, which was transported and used consistently at three sites with different atmospheric pressures: Beijing (1,014 hPa), Xining (770 hPa), and Lhasa (650 hPa). At each site, 30 analyzable lesions were obtained at each target AI value (300, 400, 500, and 600). Lesion dimensions, impedance reduction, ablation duration, temperature, and steam-pop occurrence were recorded. Differences among sites were assessed using analysis of variance and Fisher's exact test. A multiple linear regression model was constructed to evaluate the relationship between atmospheric pressure, AI, and lesion volume. At fixed AI targets, lesions created at lower-pressure sites were significantly shallower and had smaller volumes (all P   P  = 0.031). Impedance reductions differed significantly among sites at 3 and 10 s (both P   P  = 0.498). Atmospheric pressure and AI jointly explained 88.4% of the variation in lesion volume (R 2  = 0.884), enabling derivation of a hypothesis-generating AI correction equation. Within the natural range of atmospheric pressures examined, lower atmospheric pressure was associated with shallower and smaller-volume RF lesions at fixed AI targets and a higher observed incidence of steam pops. These findings suggest that atmospheric pressure may influence RF lesion formation and steam-pop occurrence, warranting further mechanistic and in vivo validation.

items.title: Joint association and interaction of lipoprotein(a) and hyperuricemia with long-term outcomes in chronic total occlusion.
items.abstract: Long-term outcomes differ substantially among patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO), and risk assessment remains challenging. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] and hyperuricemia are both associated with cardiovascular risk, but the prognostic significance of their coexistence in this population is uncertain. We retrospectively studied 391 patients with angiographically confirmed CTO. Patients were classified into four groups according to baseline Lp(a) and uric acid (UA) levels: neither elevated, elevated lipoprotein(a) only, hyperuricemia only, and both elevated. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs), defined as the first occurrence of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, target vessel revascularization, or stroke. Cox regression was used to assess long-term associations, while additive and multiplicative interactions were examined. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated using model discrimination, reclassification, calibration, and bootstrap internal validation. During a median follow-up of 73 months, event rates were 12.21%, 29.89%, 28.57%, and 66.27% across the four groups, respectively (P<0.001). Patients with both elevated lipoprotein(a) and hyperuricemia had the highest event risk compared with those with neither factor elevated (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 11.46, 95% confidence interval [CI] 6.44-20.41; P<0.001). In a sensitivity analysis restricted to all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or stroke, the association remained significant (aHR 4.23, 95% CI 2.13-8.39; P<0.001). A positive additive interaction was observed, whereas the multiplicative interaction was not significant. The apparent C-indices were 0.691 and 0.828 for the Base and Expanded models, respectively; after bootstrap optimism correction, the corresponding C-indices were 0.634 and 0.791. Concurrent elevation of Lp(a) and UA was associated with higher long-term cardiovascular risk in patients with CTO and may provide prognostic information beyond either marker considered alone. These findings require external validation before the proposed dual-biomarker classification can be applied clinically.

items.title: Predictors of nurses' management of sexual health counseling after percutaneous coronary intervention: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Sexual health counseling is a critical yet under-addressed component of cardiac rehabilitation following post-percutaneous coronary intervention. Although nurses' positive attitudes-particularly regarding role responsibility and comfort with sexual health discussions-and their readiness to provide clinical sexual counseling can facilitate patient care, translating professional knowledge into practice is often hindered by specific constraints and complex sociocultural norms. To use multiple regression analysis to identify individual and hospital ward-specific factors predicting cardiovascular nurses' sexual health care management among post-percutaneous coronary intervention patients, evaluating the incremental influences of nurses' readiness and clinical experience across departmental settings, sexual attitudes, sexual knowledge, problem-solving solutions, facilitators, and barriers. A cross-sectional, explanatory correlational study. Four tertiary-level percutaneous coronary intervention centers within the Bangkok metropolitan administration network, Bangkok, Thailand. A total of 118 cardiovascular registered nurses recruited through combined purposive and random sampling. Data were collected using validated, self-administered questionnaires. The binary sexual knowledge scale demonstrated a Kuder-Richardson Formula 20 internal consistency reliability coefficient of 0.82. The Likert-type scales exhibited Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging between 0.89 and 0.99. Content validity indices ranged from 0.90 to 0.98. Pearson's correlation coefficients were first calculated to examine bivariate relationships, followed by a three-step hierarchical multiple regression analysis to evaluate the incremental variance. The mean participants' sexual management score was 35.22±14.88 out of a possible 60 points. In the final hierarchical regression model, the combined predictors accounted for 21.6% of the total variance coefficient of determination (R 2 ) = 0.216, adjusted coefficient of determination (Adjusted R²) = .143, F-statistic (F) (10,107)  = 2.945, p  = .003). Positive sexual attitude (β = .217, p  = .019) and readiness (β = .198, p  = .030) emerged as statistically-significant positive predictors. Conversely, advanced sexual knowledge maintained a statistically-significant, counterintuitive negative association (β = -.274, p  = .003). Ward-specific analysis revealed that assignment to the outpatient department (β = -.226, p  = .020) and the cardiac catheterization laboratory (β = -.234, p  = .025) negatively predicted sexual health care management practices. Experience, sexuality education, problem-solving solutions, facilitators, and barriers were not statistically-significant. Participants' sexual management was driven by attitudes and readiness yet constrained by ward environments. Poor sexual health counseling management practices in the outpatient department and cardiac catheterization laboratory, alongside knowledge's negative impact, highlighted a "theory-practice gap." To optimize post-percutaneous coronary intervention rehabilitation in Thailand, policies should consider shifting from traditional education toward modifying workflows, establishing private counseling spaces, and developing nurse-led transitional care protocols. Not registered. (Ethical approval was prospectively obtained from the Bangkok metropolitan administration human research ethics committee [approval number COA N002hh/68_EXP] and the faculty of medicine, Vajira hospital [approval number COA 013/2568] prior to data collection).
items.journal: International journal of nursing studies advances

items.title: Knockdown of TRIM47 Attenuates Pressure Overload-Induced Heart Failure by Inhibiting NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation.
items.abstract: The ubiquitinated protein TRIM47 participates in the inflammatory regulation of various organ injuries, but its role in pressure overload-induced heart failure remains unclear. The aim of this study is to investigate the protective effect of TRIM47 knockdown against pressure overload-induced myocardial injury. A TAC mouse model of heart failure was established, and myocardial TRIM47 knockdown was achieved through targeted cardiac injection of AAV-sh-TRIM47. Heart weight/body weight ratio (HW/BW) and heart weight/tibia length ratio (HW/TL) were measured, and ANP/BNP mRNA levels were used to assess myocardial injury. HE and WGA staining were used to observe cardiomyocyte hypertrophy; Masson and Sirius red staining were used to detect myocardial fibrosis; TUNEL staining and apoptosis-related protein analysis were used to detect cardiomyocyte apoptosis; and Western blotting was used to detect the expression levels of key molecules in the NLRP3 inflammasome. TRIM47 was highly expressed in the left ventricle of mice with heart failure. In the TAC group, mice showed increased HW/BW and HW/TL ratios, as well as elevated ANP and BNP mRNA levels. Cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, disordered myofiber arrangement, increased collagen deposition and expression of fibrosis-related proteins, and myocardial apoptosis were observed. Increased expression of inflammasome activation-related proteins, including NLRP3, cleaved caspase-1, mature IL-1β, and IL-18 was also observed. Knockdown of TRIM47 reversed these pathological changes. TRIM47 is abnormally upregulated in the myocardium in pressure overload-induced heart failure. TRIM47 knockdown alleviates TAC-induced heart failure by inhibiting myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis, apoptosis, and NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

items.title: Smart biomaterials for immunomodulation in periodontitis: advances and challenges.
items.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic immunoinflammatory disease characterized by irreversible periodontal tissue destruction. Its progression is closely associated with immune dysregulation and abnormal activation of immune cell subsets. Increasing attention has been directed toward immunotherapy to improve the limited regenerative capacity of periodontal tissues. Smart biomaterials can sense local periodontal signals and produce spatiotemporal responses for controlled drug release and modulation of the immune microenvironment. However, current research mainly focuses on material design and optimization, whereas systematic comparisons and clinical evaluations of responsive systems remain insufficient. This review summarizes recent advances in smart biomaterials for periodontal immunomodulation, with emphasis on their classification based on endogenous and exogenous stimuli. Challenges involving material stability, biosafety, controlled release, and clinical translation are also discussed. This review may provide insights into the future development of immunomodulatory therapies for periodontitis.

items.title: A high-throughput functional 3D droplet microfluidic platform for function-to-transcriptome profiling identifies candidate lncRNAs associated with engineered NK cell function.
items.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cell-based immunotherapies show considerable promise for cancer treatment; however, their efficacy against solid tumors remains limited by functional heterogeneity and the restrictive tumor microenvironment. Engineered NK cells, including mesothelin-directed chimeric antigen receptor cytokine-induced memory-like (MSLN-CAR CIML) NK cells, exhibit enhanced cytotoxic potential, yet the transcriptional programs underlying effective tumor killing remain poorly defined. Although protein-coding regulators of NK cell function have been extensively studied, the contribution of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to cytotoxic NK cell states remains largely unexplored, particularly in engineered NK cell therapies. To address this gap, we developed and applied a three-dimensional (3D) Matrigel-based droplet microfluidic screening platform that enables single-cell resolution analysis of NK-tumor interactions. Unlike conventional bulk transcriptomic approaches, this function-to-transcriptome workflow enables functional isolation of killer and non-killer NK cell populations prior to transcriptomic profiling enabling the direct comparison of transcriptional programs associated with cytotoxic function while minimizing confounding effects of bulk population analyses. Using this approach, we profiled donor-matched MSLN-CAR CIML NK cells and CIML NK controls from three independent donors. Comparative transcriptomic analysis revealed widespread differences in lncRNA expression between killer and non-killer NK cell populations, characterized predominantly by broad lncRNA downregulation that was consistently observed across donors and more pronounced in MSLN-CAR CIML NK cells than in CIML controls. Integrated lncRNA-mRNA analyses prioritized candidate lncRNA-gene pairs based on genomic proximity and coordinated co-expression patterns, identifying several lncRNAs associated with cytotoxic gene programs. These transcriptional signatures were further associated with enrichment of cytotoxic and inflammatory pathways characteristic of highly functional NK cell states. Together, these findings demonstrate the utility of our functional droplet microfluidic screening platform in prioritizing candidate lncRNAs associated with cytotoxic NK cell states within matrix-restricted tumor environments. By integrating functional phenotyping with transcriptomic profiling, this platform provides a framework for identifying candidate lncRNA and other potential biomarkers associated with cytotoxic NK states for future mechanistic validation and the rational optimization of NK cell-based immunotherapies for solid tumors.

items.title: Morusin induces GSDME-dependent pyroptosis in non-small cell lung cancer via the angiotensin II receptor type 2.
items.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, its 5-year survival rate continues to be unsatisfactory. Current therapies are often limited by resistance, toxicity, or poor efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for novel strategies. We performed a high-throughput compound screen for inducing cell death in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells. Combined with lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release assays, cell death morphology observation, and propidium iodide (PI) staining, we confirmed the cell death mode as pyroptosis. Then, we conducted a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen to identify the critical regulator of compound-induced pyroptosis. The screening results showed that morusin is a trigger of gasdermin E (GSDME)-mediated pyroptosis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells. Importantly, morusin suppresses tumor growth in vivo . Through a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen, we further demonstrated that angiotensin II receptor type 2 (AGTR2) as a critical regulator of morusin-induced pyroptosis, acting via activation of the caspase-3-GSDME signaling cascade. Notably, morusin also upregulated AGTR2 expression in NSCLC cells. In an NSCLC mouse model, morusin treatment potently suppressed wild-type tumor growth, whereas its antitumor efficacy was substantially diminished in AGTR2-knockout tumors. Our study reveals a novel mechanism underlying the antitumor effect of morusin, establishes AGTR2 as a potential therapeutic target, and provides a rationale for pyroptosis-based therapy for NSCLC.

items.title: A single-cell transcriptomics-based prognostic model identifies TM4SF1 as a key promoter of malignant progression in lung adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Intratumor heterogeneity in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) profoundly influences tumor progression and immune evasion. However, current prognostic models largely fail to capture the complex cellular dynamics of the tumor microenvironment (TME) at single-cell resolution. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing with bulk transcriptomics to derive cell-type-specific signatures. A systematic evaluation of 101 machine learning algorithm combinations was performed across multiple independent cohorts to construct a robust prognostic model. Immune landscape, mutational features, intercellular communication, and immunotherapy responsiveness were comprehensively evaluated. The biological functions of the identified hub gene, transmembrane 4 L six family member 1 (TM4SF1), were rigorously validated in vitro . The optimal StepCox[forward]-Ridge model showed strong prognostic stratification in five cohorts. Low-risk tumors exhibited an immune-inflamed phenotype, suggesting greater predicted good responses to immune checkpoint blockade. In contrast, high-risk tumors had an immunosuppressive TME with overactive cell communication driven by fibroblasts and myeloid cells. TM4SF1 was a key driver in this high-risk signature. TM4SF1 silencing significantly inhibited LUAD cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and strongly induced apoptosis. TM4SF1 depletion reversed tumor immune evasion by reducing PD-L1, increasing MHC-I, and lowering the secretion of CCL5. This single-cell-guided machine-learning framework provides strong prognostic stratification in LUAD and captures immune phenotypes associated with potential immunotherapy responsiveness. TM4SF1 emerged as a candidate mediator associated with malignant progression and immune-related phenotypes in LUAD, warranting further mechanistic and in vivo investigation. This suggests it could be a useful therapeutic target.

items.title: Case Report: Glofitamab and intrathecal rituximab combined with ICE chemotherapy for early isolated central nervous system relapse in pediatric Burkitt lymphoma: rapid clearance and successful bridging to autologous stem cell transplantation.
items.abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) relapse is an uncommon and highly aggressive event in pediatric Burkitt lymphoma (BL), particularly when occurring early with parenchymal involvement. Despite CNS-directed chemotherapy, rapid and durable disease control remains challenging. Glofitamab, a CD20×CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, has shown activity in relapsed/refractory B-cell lymphomas, but its role in pediatric BL with CNS relapse remains unexplored. Intrathecal rituximab provides direct CNS delivery of anti-CD20 antibody. We treated a child with early isolated CNS relapse of BL using systemic glofitamab combined with intrathecal rituximab. An 11-year-old boy with stage IV, R4-group BL involving bone marrow and CNS achieved complete remission after frontline CCCG-BNHL-2015 therapy. Three months after treatment cessation, he developed headache, vomiting, and blurred vision. Brain MRI showed multiple parenchymal CNS lesions, while bone marrow and thoracoabdominal imaging revealed no systemic relapse. CSF flow cytometry showed an abnormal B-cell population comprising 44.63% of nucleated cells, confirming early isolated CNS relapse. The patient received three cycles of ICE chemotherapy combined with glofitamab, along with seven administrations of intrathecal rituximab and four administrations of triple intrathecal chemotherapy. Glofitamab was administered with obinutuzumab pretreatment and step-up dosing, while intrathecal rituximab was combined with methotrexate, cytarabine, and dexamethasone. Neurological symptoms improved rapidly, and CSF abnormal B cells decreased from 44.63% to undetectable levels within 10 days. He subsequently underwent CNS-directed radiotherapy and autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Serial CSF flow cytometry remained negative, and follow-up brain MRI showed no active disease. The patient remains in continuous complete remission. Systemic glofitamab combined with intrathecal rituximab may represent a feasible compartment-adapted strategy for early isolated CNS relapse of pediatric BL. Although the individual contributions of the treatment components cannot be determined because of concomitant therapies, rapid CSF clearance within 10 days enabled subsequent consolidation with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. To our knowledge, this is the first reported use of this combination in pediatric BL with isolated CNS relapse, supporting further investigation of bispecific antibody-based immunotherapy combined with CNS-directed therapy.

items.title: Clinical and microbiological characterization of Starmerella magnoliae in the female genital tract: case report and diagnostic challenges.
items.abstract: Starmerella magnoliae (formerly Candida magnoliae ) is a rare yeast in clinical practice, sporadically associated with neonatal bloodstream infections, tenosynovitis in immunocompetent individuals, and infections in oncology patients. Its role in female genital tract infections is exceptionally uncommon. We describe a 42-year-old Brazilian woman presenting with genital pruritus and burning. Serological tests for HIV, hepatitis B and C, syphilis, and HPV RT-PCR were negative. Vaginal samples were cultured, identified using the Vitek 2 system (bioMérieux, France), and confirmed by MALDI-TOF MS. Antifungal resistance-associated genes were investigated by polymerase chain reaction.Culture identified S. magnoliae . Metabolic profiling demonstrated assimilation of raffinose, proline, mannose, sorbitol, nitrate, gluconate, and gentiobiose. Molecular analysis detected ERG11 and CDR2 genes associated with antifungal resistance. Empirical oral fluconazole therapy failed to achieve clinical improvement. However, intravaginal nystatin administered for 21 days resulted in complete symptom resolution and negative direct microscopy. This case underscores S. magnoliae as a rare cause of vulvovaginal infection, associated with azole resistance markers and poor response to fluconazole. Accurate identification using advanced microbiological and molecular methods is essential to guide appropriate therapy in uncommon infections.

items.title: Hydrogen Sulfide, a Potential Novel Drug, Attenuates Concanavalin A-Induced Hepatitis [Retraction].
Posttransplant Diabetes Mellitus in Kidney Transplant Recipients Across the Arab World: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Precision-Risk Framework.
items.abstract: Posttransplant diabetes mellitus is a key complication after kidney transplant, linked to increased cardiovascular, infection, graft loss, and death risks. Regional data on posttransplant diabetes mellitus remain absent in the Arab world. Regional factors like consanguinity, pharmacogenomics, and hypomagnesemia are not included in current risk models. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA 2020 and MOOSE guidelines, registered with PROSPERO. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science through March 1, 2025, for studies involving adult Arab kidney transplant recipients without preexisting diabetes. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated 12-month posttransplant diabetes mellitus incidence and risk factors. We also assessed evidence certainty. Our analyses included 16 studies comprising 3622 kidney transplant recipients from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Egypt, Sudan, and multicenter Arab cohorts. The pooled 12-month incidence of post-transplant diabetes mellitus was 19.8% (95% CI, 16.2-23.8%; I² = 89% ). Significant risk factors (as shown by odds ratio) included age per decade (1.49), body mass index ≥25 kg/m² (1.92), prediabetes (4.28), hypertension (2.56), hepatitis C virus seropositivity (2.31), and hypomagnesemia <1.9 mg/dL (5.11), with tacrolimus versus cyclosporine showing marginal increase in risk; exclusion of a Sudanese outlier strengthened this association but remained lower than in Western populations. No study evaluated consanguinity. Evidence certainty ranged from moderate (for age, body mass index, hypertension, and hepatitis C virus) to low/very low for other factors. Although traditional risk factors for posttransplant diabetes mellitus remain relevant, tacrolimus showed a weaker association, possibly due to genetic variants such as CYP3A5. Hypomagnesemia represented a key modifiable risk factor. Our findings support a precision-risk framework that incorporates regional data and call for multicenter Arab registries integrating genomics, glycemia, and machine learning to improve risk stratification of posttransplant diabetes mellitus. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate findings and establish causal relationships.

items.title: Seroprevalence update of Hepatitis B Virus, Hepatitis C Virus, and human immunodeficiency virus among people who inject drugs in Kuwait: a cross-sectional study at a national addiction treatment center.
items.abstract: People who inject drugs (PWID) represent a key population disproportionately affected by blood-borne viruses. Updated epidemiological data are crucial for informing public health interventions. This study provides a 2024 update on the seroprevalence and correlates of Hepatitis B (HBV), Hepatitis C (HCV), and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) among PWID at Kuwait's national addiction treatment center, building on a previous 2017 baseline. A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to December 2024, enrolling 1,287 consecutive patients. Serological screening for HBsAg, anti-HCV, and anti-HIV was performed using chemiluminescent immunoassays. Seropositive samples underwent confirmatory nucleic acid testing to detect active viremia. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with each infection. The cohort was predominantly male (86.6%) and Kuwaiti (87.3%), with a median age of 33 years. The overall seroprevalence was 0.2% for HBsAg (2/1,255), 2.1% for anti-HCV (25/1,169), and 0.93% for anti-HIV (12/1,287). A significant age-dependent increase in HCV prevalence was observed (p < 0.001), with the highest prevalence (10.8%) in participants aged ≥ 50 years. All HIV-positive cases were male. Molecular testing revealed universal active viremia for HCV (100%, 25/25) and HBV (100%, 2/2), and detectable viremia in 66.7% (8/12) of HIV-seropositive cases. In multivariable analysis, increasing age was significantly associated with HCV infection (aOR = 1.1, 95% CI: 1.07-1.16, p < 0.001). For HIV, female sex was associated with significantly lower odds of infection (aOR = 0.14, 95% CI: 0.02-0.92, p = 0.04). Due to the extremely low number of HBV-reactive cases (n = 2), multivariable logistic regression was not feasible for HBV, and no adjusted estimates could be derived. Compared to 2017 data, this study reveals a concerning increase in HIV prevalence and a shift to universal active HCV viremia among PWID in Kuwait. The near-ubiquitous presence of transmissible infection upon seroconversion indicates a critical gap in the care cascade. These findings underscore an urgent need for the scale-up of targeted harm reduction, test-and-treat strategies, and integrated care services to curb transmission.

items.title: Case Report: Durable response to tislelizumab monotherapy in microsatellite-stable, BRAF V600E-mutant right-sided colon cancer with extremely high PD-L1 expression.
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer with proficient mismatch repair (pMMR)/microsatellite stable (MSS) status is generally intrinsically resistant to immune checkpoint inhibitors; tumors with concomitant BRAF V600E mutations are highly aggressive, and conventional chemotherapy and targeted therapies have limited efficacy, resulting in a lack of effective personalized treatment options in clinical practice. This report describes a case of locally advanced right-sided colon adenocarcinoma that was pMMR/MSS, harbored a BRAF V600E mutation, and exhibited high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression (tumor proportion score [TPS] > 95%). The patient developed intestinal obstruction after failure of first-line conversion therapy. After undergoing palliative gastrojejunostomy and cecostomy, she developed gastroparesis and a liver abscess. Given the extremely high PD-L1 expression, tislelizumab monotherapy was initiated before the patient's general condition had fully recovered. After three cycles, the patient's performance status improved significantly. She then received a combination of tislelizumab and raltitrexed for two cycles; however, chemotherapy was discontinued due to raltitrexed-induced liver injury, and the patient continued maintenance therapy with tislelizumab monotherapy, achieving a partial response (PR) as the best outcome. After nine cycles of maintenance therapy, a new mass appeared in the right adnexal region, indicating disease progression; the overall progression-free survival (PFS) was 14 months. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of a patient with colorectal adenocarcinoma harboring a BRAF V600E mutation, characterized by extremely high PD-L1 expression and pMMR/MSS status, who achieved a PR with a regimen centered on programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor monotherapy. This case suggests that for BRAF V600E-mutated colorectal cancer, assessment of PD-L1 expression levels should be considered regardless of mismatch repair status; if extremely high PD-L1 expression is present, even in the pMMR/MSS phenotype, PD-1 inhibitors may offer a potential personalized treatment option for these patients with poor prognosis and limited therapeutic choices.

items.title: Influence of the initial recurrence and metastatic site on outcomes in postoperative gastric cancer patients.
items.abstract: To evaluate the impact of initial recurrence and metastatic sites on survival outcomes in gastric cancer patients after radical gastrectomy. A retrospective study was conducted on 1,140 patients with pathologically confirmed gastric cancer who underwent radical gastrectomy between September 2016 and December 2023. Patients were categorized into six groups according to initial recurrence and recurrence site: no recurrence, local recurrence, liver metastasis, peritoneal/retroperitoneal metastasis, multiple-site peritoneal metastasis, and other sites. Overall survival (OS) and Post-Recurrence Survival (PRS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and log-ran k tests. Independent prognostic factors were identified by Cox regression. Age ≥60 years, CEA ≥5U/ml, pathological type (other), T4 Stage, perineural invasion and lymphovascular invasion were independent risk factors for poor OS, while middle-third and lower-third gastric location were protective factors. As for DFS, tumor differentiation, lymph node metastasis, perineural invasion, and site of recurrence/metastasis were significantly associated with the PRS. In the multivariable analysis, only perineural invasion remained an independent risk factor for PRS ( HR  = 1.588, P = 0.005). Among 222 patients with recurrence, patients with Multiple-site peritoneal metastasis had the numerically shortest median OS (20 months, 95% CI 17.040-22.960) among the five recurrence subgroups. No statistically significant between-group differences were identified after Bonferroni correction for 10 pairwise log-rank comparisons. PRS was longest in liver metastasis patients (10 months), significantly longer than multiple-site peritoneal metastasis (3 months, P   P  = 0.028). Comprehensive therapy was associated with significantly longer PRS compared with supportive care (9 vs. 3 months, P   P  = 0.002). PRS differed among patients with different initial recurrence/metastatic patterns. However, the initial recurrence/metastatic site was not independently associated with PRS. Perineural invasion was independently associated with shorter PRS and OS and may serve as a reference factor for post-recurrence prognostic assessment. Patients receiving comprehensive therapy after recurrence showed longer PRS.

items.title: Potential symptom management targets following transarterial chemoembolization in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: a network analysis and computer-simulation study.
items.abstract: Potential symptom intervention targets in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) remain poorly understood. Symptom network analysis combined with computer-simulated interventions may help identify priority targets for symptom management. To examine symptom associations and explore potential symptom management targets among patients with HCC following TACE. A cross-sectional study included 312 patients with HCC. Symptoms were assessed 24-48 h after TACE using the Chinese versions of the M. D. Anderson Symptom Inventory and the primary liver cancer-specific symptom module. A Gaussian graphical model was used to examine symptom associations, while an Ising model and NodeIdentifyR algorithm were used to explore simulated symptom perturbations. Fatigue (86.5%), disturbed sleep (83.7%), and lack of appetite (75.0%) were the most prevalent symptoms. Nausea showed the highest estimated strength centrality. Hypothetical alleviation of dry mouth produced the largest model-predicted decrease in the mean number of active symptoms, whereas hypothetical aggravation of fever produced the largest increase. Nausea was the most connected symptom according to estimated strength centrality. Dry mouth and fever showed the largest model-predicted responses to alleviating and aggravating threshold perturbations, respectively. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation; they do not establish clinical treatment effects.

items.title: The Fourth WANA International Congress on "Stem Cells in Regenerative Medicine": A Brief Report.
items.abstract: The 4 th West Asia and North Africa (WANA) International Congress, held on May 3-4, 2025 in Kish Island (Iran), was a significant event organized by the Royan Institute in collaboration with domestic and international partners. It gathered the leading experts in stem cell research, regenerative medicine and industry to discuss the latest advances in these fields, and strategize overcoming scientific and clinical challenges specific to the WANA region. The congress showcased a dynamic mix of plenary sessions, workshops, and exhibitions highlighting cutting-edge innovations from science-based companies, fostering international collaboration and knowledge exchange. Key Highlights included breakthroughs in liver regenerative medicine using adult stem/progenitor cells, dopaminergic progenitor cell transplantation for Parkinson disease, stem cell-mediated hearing regeneration, and novel approaches to osteoarthritis (OA) and cancer therapy. The event also emphasized the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) and computational biology in drug discovery, research transparency, and personalized therapies through multi-omics profiling. This article highlights the congress scientific initiatives in stem cell research, showcasing recent advancements, new opportunities, and obstacles in turning research into clinical practice, while highlighting the importance of regional cooperation in fostering innovation within regenerative medicine.

items.title: Past, present and future of Estetrol (E4); a natural fetal estrogen for human use.
items.abstract: Estetrol (E4) is a natural estrogen produced by the fetal liver with a distinctive pharmacologic profile separating it from other natural and synthetic estrogens. Encompassing 25 years of research and development, this review summarizes the history, biochemistry, pharmacology, clinical development, and potential future applications of E4. Essential features of E4 are (1) its high oral bioavailability, long half-life and minimal binding to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), enabling once-daily oral use, and (2) the limited effects on liver function, especially on hemostatic factors, resulting in a lower risk of venous thromboembolism compared to other natural and synthetic estrogens. Estetrol is further characterized as a natural estrogen with selective tissue activity, with a limited impact on breast tissue and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters, while preserving efficacy including bone mass protection. Estetrol therefore has the potential for a markedly improved safety profile. Clinically, the E4/drospirenone (DRSP) combined oral contraceptive (COC) is available worldwide since 2022 and provides effective contraception, a predictable bleeding profile, and a favorable tolerability profile. In phase 2 and 3 studies in postmenopausal women, oral E4 improves vasomotor symptoms, vaginal and urogenital complaints, and quality of life and wellbeing. Ongoing research is exploring wider uses, including combination with the oral GnRH antagonist relugolix for a COC with a focus on the perimenopausal transition and possible applications of E4 in gynecology, endocrinology, obstetrics, neurology and oncology, especially the treatment of advanced breast and prostate cancer.
